correctness.rationale: With positive switching rates and at least one positive harmonic stiffness, both the first-moment tilted generator Q-K and the second-moment generator Q-2K are stable. The stationary state-conditioned second moments satisfy (2K-Q)u=2Dp; the exact covariance and additive-drift impulse response are 1^T exp[(Q-K)t]u and 1^T exp[(Q-K)t]p. Their FDT-form defect is a sum of the two distinct negative exponential modes, and the stationary Ito balance gives F(0)=0. Direct algebra gives F'(0)=Dab(k1-k0)^2/[(a+b)Z]. These two initial conditions uniquely determine the closed formula. Positivity, unique maximum, finite integral, and k0=0 cancellation follow without approximations. The actual companion Python implementation independently evaluates all matrices and the formula for 960 parameter/time cases, 160 sums and peaks, and two Monte Carlo samples; finite checks supplement but do not establish the proof.

value.rationale: The problem is physically motivated by randomly controlled optical traps: displacement relaxation and externally forced susceptibility may look compatible with equilibrium at individual observables, yet their exact gap is strictly signed across every positive lag. Measuring two time-domain observables rather than stationary moments is a substantive diagnostic of nonequilibrium; the closed integrated sum rule is unexpectedly insensitive to how strong the on trap is, in a broad asymmetric-switching regime. The theorem resolves the natural complete sign/peak/area classification for this scalar two-state model rather than an arbitrary unmotivated numerical slice.
